[8:56AM] #Iju_Ishaga #TrafficUpdate 

Fagba Intersection is currently very busy inward Agege Pen Cinema as a result of the morning rush, while traffic flow inward Amala remains free. Movement from Jonathan Coker back to Fagba is steady this morning.

Along Iju Road down to Agege Pen Cinema, traffic is generally good, though slightly busy before the bridge. The return journey via College traffic light is smooth, and movement along Hospital Road down to African Church is also good.

Idi Agbon, Haruna, and Oyemekun corridors are experiencing good flow, though there is a slight slowdown before the traffic light at Yaya Abatan. Ajayi is moving well, with a fast return to Jungle, while inward Fagba remains smooth.

Traffic from Fagba inward Ishaga is also free, and the return journey from Ishaga up to Alamutu is fast, with steady movement back to Fagba Intersection. Officers are currently positioned at various choke points, actively managing traffic.

No impediments reported at this time, and our men are present at important locations ensuring ease of movement.

#FollowLASTMA

Traffic Advisory

09 September 2025

ONGOING PROTEST ACTION IN IVORY AND EBONY PARK, MIDRAND 

The Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD) officers are monitoring an ongoing protest in Ivory and Ebony Park, Midrand. 

Residents are allegedly protesting over prolonged water outages in the area and have barricaded off Republic Road with burning tyres, rocks, and debris. 

The situation remains calm despite the road closures. Motorists are urged to exercise caution when travelling in the area, avoid Republic Road and use alternative routes.

-END-

Issued by the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department Communication Unit ##SaferJoburg #NomakanjaniManjeNamhlanje #JoburgRoadSafety #JHBTraffic

PRESS RELEASE — Ikogosi Marathon 2025 (2nd Edition)

The Ikogosi Marathon Initiative, in partnership with the Government of Ekiti State, has announced the 2nd Edition of the Ikogosi 17.5km Marathon, scheduled for Saturday, November 8, 2025.

At the inaugural press conference held on September 8, 2025, the Governor of Ekiti State, represented by the Technical Advisor on Sports Development, Dr. Olusola Osetoba, reaffirmed the government’s full support for the marathon, describing it as a flagship project for sports development, tourism promotion, and youth empowerment.

The marathon will hold on Saturday, November 8, 2025, with the race starting promptly at 7:00 AM from the Ilawe-Ekiti Roundabout (in front of the Alawe Palace) and finishing at the Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort. Organizers expect between 4,000 and 5,000 participants from across Nigeria and abroad, building on the success of the previous edition which attracted over 2,200 runners.

Registration is already open and will close on November 1, 2025. Interested participants can register online via https://t.co/1FuQkS2UDA, while forms are also available at the offices of Local Government Chairmen across Ekiti State. Every registered runner will receive a goody bag containing a running vest, number bib, race information leaflet, refreshments, and a finishing medal.

Attractive prizes have been announced to reward excellence and participation. For the Elite Category (Male & Female), the first prize winner will take home ₦2,000,000, while the second and third place winners will receive ₦1,500,000 and ₦1,000,000 respectively. For the Indigenous Category (Male & Female), the first prize winner will go home with ₦1,500,000, the second prize is ₦1,000,000, and the third prize is ₦500,000. The fourth place winner will receive ₦250,000, the fifth place ₦100,000, while those who finish between sixth and tenth position will each earn ₦50,000.

We have assured that all necessary safety and logistical arrangements have been made. The race will take place on a certified route with refreshment points along the way. Full security coverage will be provided in partnership with the Nigeria Police and Civil Defence, while emergency response teams and ambulances will be stationed along the route. In addition, a traffic advisory has been issued to notify the public that all routes within the race corridor will be closed during the marathon, with alternative routes advised. To ease access, shuttle buses will convey runners from all 16 Local Government Headquarters across Ekiti State as well as from the Pavilion in Ado Ekiti to the starting point, and will return participants to their respective locations after the race.

The Ikogosi Marathon is more than a sporting event. It is a platform to promote the Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort as a global tourist attraction, boost local businesses, encourage fitness and healthy living, and provide youth with opportunities through NYSC volunteers, race marshals, and community engagement.

The organizers expressed their appreciation to the Governor and Government of Ekiti State for their unwavering support, and also extended gratitude to early sponsors and partners. They further called on corporate organizations across banking, telecoms, beverage, and transport sectors to partner in making the Ikogosi Marathon 2025 a landmark event.

Read the full press release and register now: https://t.co/1FuQkS2UDA

#IkogosiMarathon2025 #EkitiRising #SportsTourism #RunEkiti

data.raw_text:
🚨 Flood Control Scam: The Biggest Corruption Case Yet

Philippines has seen its share of scandals — Fertilizer Fund (₱728M, Arroyo era), PDAF “pork barrel” (₱10B, Aquino era)… but the Flood Control scam dwarfs them all.

💸 Since 2022, ₱545B+ went into flood projects.
👉 Many are overpriced, ghost, or shoddily built.
👉 Only 15 contractors bagged 20% of the budget.
👉 Kickbacks of 25–50% per project.

📌 Testimony reveals lawmakers demanded kickbacks; DPWH officials signed off on fake or incomplete works. Ghost projects = billions lost while communities drown.

🔎 Scale of Scams

Fertilizer Fund: ₱728M

PDAF: ₱10B

Flood Control: ₱100B–₱500B+

This is corruption on a historic scale.

---

🛑 Why can’t PH minimize corruption?

Budget insertions = lawmakers funneling projects to cronies.

DPWH collusion = rubber-stamped “completion” papers.

Weak enforcement = cases drag, few punished.

Political dynasties = recycling the same names, same rackets.

---

💡 Bottom line: Until Congress loses its power to insert projects & agencies enforce real accountability, scams like these will keep flooding the Philippines — literally and financially.

#Corruption #FloodControlScam #Philippines
